subject: Cognitive Science
title: The Sunk Cost Fallacy
description: A quick, practical guide to The Sunk Cost Fallacy.

hook.text: You've watched 90 minutes of a terrible film. You stay because you've 'already invested the time.'

buildup.text: The sunk cost fallacy: past investments—time, money, effort—shouldn't affect future decisions, but they do.

discovery.text: Rationally, only future costs and benefits matter. The money already spent is gone regardless.

twist.text: Businesses sink billions into failing projects because leaders won't abandon their prior commitments.

climax.text: The Concorde jet was continued for decades despite guaranteed losses—now economists call it the Concorde fallacy.

punchline.text: What you've spent shouldn't decide what you do next.

quiz.question: What is the sunk cost fallacy?
options: Letting past investment drive future decisions
